power_telemetry_logger: smoothen out NaN values if possible This change adds a thin wrapper around numpy.interp to interpolate missing power data. It also introduces the policy that any array with a higher ratio than X where X is set to 0.1 will cause the power test to fail as this is likely a bigger issue than some one-off readings failing. Additionally, if there are more than Y, where Y is set to 5, consecutive NaN readings, the test will also fail. Lastly, it adds unit-tests for the data interpolation logic. power: Fix up power supplies for 4.19+ kernels In older kernels, /sys/class/power_supply/<instance/type had fairly dynamic contents that indicated whether or not the power supply was USB dual role. In 4.19 kernels, this file is very static, and for Chrome OS EC USB ports, just has "USB" in it. Instead, a new "usb_type" file is present that has the dual-role info in it. It comes in a form like this, with brackets around the selected one: Unknown SDP DCP CDP C PD [PD_DRP] BrickID If the type file has "USB" in it, attempt to access usb_type. If it works and what's selected is PD_DRP, then use this as an indication of a dual-role port. BUG=b:123541187 TEST=Plug in another chromebook via type-C, observe dropdown in Settings>Power. Tested on Hatch and Kohaku. Change-Id: Ifaac85c81842f6643be92d681ce69550bf5e0e43 Signed-off-by: Evan Green <evgreen@chromium.org> Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1684359 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Ravi Chandra Sadineni <ravisadineni@chromium.org>

CHROMIUM: config: Turn off Rockchip crypto for arm64 Rockchip crypto is not a win on arm64 devices--it's better to use the normal arm64 crypto. See the linked bug. Let's turn it off. echo 'CONFIG_CRYPTO_DEV_ROCKCHIP=n' >> \ chromeos/config/arm64/chromiumos-arm64.flavour.config echo 'CONFIG_CRYPTO_DEV_ROCKCHIP=n' >> \ chromeos/config/arm64/chromiumos-rockchip64.flavour.config ./chromeos/scripts/kernelconfig olddefconfig NOTES: - actually this CL is a no-op (other than shrinking the kernel) since the crypto isn't enabled in the device tree anyway. - according to an email I have from Collabora there were some problems with the Rockchip crypto driver on arm64; not sure if that got fixed. The email I have said "The I/O helper is wrong in this driver, because it's not really I/O memory, but just 32-bit registers, and so 64-bit accessess don't work." - it seems like it _could_ be plausible that someone might someday find a way to use Rockchip's acceleration in conjunction with the normal arm64 crypto. If/when that days comes, we can always turn this back on. BUG=b:35579274 TEST=None Change-Id: Ifca50cd40fb0fdb3caa5b95585b7cf29cddf62b0 Signed-off-by: Douglas Anderson <dianders@chromium.org> (cherry picked from commit e321a30fd3144ea8e99014bd608cd5121afb4422) Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/1693713 Legacy-Commit-Queue: Commit Bot <commit-bot@chromium.org> Reviewed-by: Brian Norris <briannorris@chromium.org>

CRAS: a2dp_iodev - Fix socket depth frames We use setsockopt to configure the A2DP socket depth (i.e the maximum send buffer of socket). However kernel has its own logic to determine the actual final value, and it may not equal to what we set. According to net/core/sock.c Fix A2DP socket depth by using getsockopt to query the actual value. This will make our A2DP delay report more accurate. BUG=b:132130485 TEST=Test Sony WH-1000Xm3 headset on Atlas, this change corrects about 3000 frames of delay. Launch AV sync video on web based YouTube to verify the sync is a lot better.
